fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff's allegations of retaliation for complaining about odors in her apartment fail to state a plausible FHA retaliation claim under § 3617 because complaints about general housing conditions are not complaints about unlawful discrimination. The FHA anti-retaliation provision protects only against retaliation for reporting discriminatory housing practices, not general maintenance or habitability issues.

case_name: Quinn Ngiendo v. Pep-KU, LLC, Amelia Ludlow, Madison Cline and Lucy Evans
key_cases_cited: Ashcroft v. Iqbal, 556 U.S. 662 (2009)

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to plausibly allege that the alleged hostile housing environment was severe and pervasive or motivated by race. The court found the allegations (spoiled milk, hidden remote, loud music, rude comments) described isolated, boorish behavior insufficient under Iqbal/Twombly to state a plausible claim of racial discrimination.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Eviction based on race or national origin
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to plausibly allege racial motivation for eviction. A stray remark by a manager asking where plaintiff was from, combined with unrelated incidents of rudeness, was too isolated and ambiguous to nudge the claim from possibility to plausibility under Iqbal/Twombly.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Discriminatory advertising showing preference for white tenants
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff's allegations regarding pool parties and advertisements showing white tenants were too vague and conclusory to plausibly describe a violation of 42 U.S.C. § 3604(c). The complaint lacked specific facts about actual advertisements indicating racial preference.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Eviction in retaliation for complaining about racial harassment and loud music
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to plausibly allege retaliation under § 3617. The alleged conduct (loud music with offensive lyrics, malicious statements) did not constitute a violation of the Fair Housing Act itself, and plaintiff did not allege facts showing when or to whom she made a protected complaint before the eviction was initiated.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Lenient application of lease terms and noise accommodation for fibromyalgia and post-traumatic stress sensitivity to noise
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to plausibly allege a disability claim under 42 U.S.C. § 3602(h). The complaint did not allege facts showing that fibromyalgia or post-traumatic stress substantially limited major life activities, that plaintiff had a record of such impairment, or that the landlord knew of or was requested to provide an accommodation.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: State law claims including tortious interference with contract and personal injury
fha_claims.reasoning: The court declined to exercise supplemental jurisdiction over state law claims because all federal FHA claims were dismissed before trial, and judicial economy, convenience, fairness and comity favored declining jurisdiction.

case_name: Quinn Ngiendo v. University Partners, LLC
key_cases_cited: Ashcroft v. Iqbal, 556 U.S. 662 (2009)

Cinnamon Hills Youth Crisis Ctr., Inc. v. Saint George City, 685 F.3d 917 (10th Cir. 2012)

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Intervention in neighbors' noisemaking and removal of neighbors to accommodate PTSD sensitivity to noise
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to plausibly allege a reasonable accommodation. Seeking eviction of neighbors or soundproofing is not a reasonable accommodation under the FHA; the court found these requests implausible as a matter of law.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Inspection of unit before occupancy and mold removal/cleaning to accommodate rhinitis triggered by mold and allergens
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff plausibly alleged all five elements of an FHA reasonable accommodation claim: handicap (rhinitis substantially limiting breathing), defendant knowledge, necessity of accommodation, reasonableness of the request (unit inspection and mold removal), and defendant's refusal. The court rejected defendants' arguments that FHA does not apply to use and enjoyment or that lack of maintenance is not an FHA claim.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Holdover tenancy to remain in apartment despite lease expiration due to frozen shoulder (adhesive capsulitis) injury
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to plausibly allege a reasonable accommodation. Indefinite holdover tenancy based on physical handicap is not a recognized reasonable accommodation under the FHA. Additionally, plaintiff provided only threadbare recitals of the extent of the shoulder injury without sufficient factual support. Dismissed with prejudice as futile amendment.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Accommodation for sciatica nerve condition causing limping, including removal of welcome desk on sidewalk, elimination of sprinklers on sidewalk, and removal of school bus blocking handicap access
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to plausibly allege multiple elements: no facts showing sciatica substantially limits a major life activity; no allegation that University Partners knew of the disability; and no showing that accommodation was necessary (one incident of tripping and inconvenience from wet sidewalks do not meet the 'indispensable' standard). Dismissed with prejudice as futile amendment.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Retaliation for seeking accommodation for rhinitis by placement in moldy unit and delayed maintenance
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff plausibly alleged all three elements of FHA retaliation: protected activity (seeking accommodation for rhinitis), adverse action (placement in moldy unit and delayed maintenance), and causal link (close temporal proximity between accommodation requests and adverse actions). Timing inference supports retaliation claim at pleading stage.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Retaliation for seeking accommodation for rhinitis by placement in moldy unit and delayed maintenance at Everest property
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff plausibly alleged all three elements of FHA retaliation against Everest: protected activity (seeking accommodation for rhinitis), adverse action (placement in moldy unit and delayed maintenance in October), and causal link (close temporal proximity—one month after moving in and requesting mold cleanup).

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Intentional discrimination based on race (Black) and national origin (Kenya) in terms and conditions of rental
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff plausibly alleged disparate treatment claim against Asset by connecting her terrible living conditions (moldy, filthy apartment) to her race and national origin with more than sheer speculation, noting that white tenants had better housing while she and minority roommates were in a moldy unit.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Intentional discrimination based on race and national origin in denial of lease renewal
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff's single-paragraph allegation that University Partners' refusal to allow holdover tenancy was motivated by race and national origin improperly relied on sheer speculation without factual support connecting the denial to protected class status.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Hostile housing environment based on race created by upstairs neighbor's harassment (racial epithets, door kicking, knife stabbing, blocking paths) with Everest's knowledge and inaction
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to plausibly allege that Everest knew or should have known about race-based harassment by the neighbor. Conclusory statements that Everest 'knew about' harassment and that incidents were 'brought to its attention' are not entitled to presumption of truth. Plaintiff did not allege specific facts showing Everest's actual knowledge of racial harassment.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: State law claims (tort, breach of contract, and other state-based causes of action)
fha_claims.reasoning: Court declined to dismiss state law claims under 28 U.S.C. § 1367(c)(3) because not all federal claims were dismissed and the state claims remain part of the same case or controversy as the surviving federal claims against other defendants.

case_name: Quinn Ngiendo v. University Partners, LLC

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Hostile housing environment based on race and national origin; failure to remedy harassment by other tenants including knife attack and racial vandalism
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to plausibly allege that Waypoint knew or should have known she was subjected to harassment based on race or national origin. Conclusory allegations that Waypoint was aware of harassment are not entitled to presumption of truth under Iqbal. The only specific facts alleged—a request for a police report and emails about another tenant's vandalism—are insufficient to show Waypoint knew of race-based harassment against plaintiff.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Intentional infliction of emotional distress (University Partners); intentional and negligent infliction of emotional distress (Waypoint); negligent failure to hire and supervise real estate agents
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to plausibly allege the elements of intentional infliction of emotional distress against University Partners (no facts showing intentional or reckless conduct by defendant). Against Waypoint, plaintiff made only conclusory assertions about negligent infliction of emotional distress without alleging any facts supporting the required elements (physical injury, direct causation, temporal proximity).

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Permission to retain a two-bedroom apartment to provide a separate bedroom for plaintiff's nighttime aide(s) to sleep while providing Enhanced Care Services (non-nursing physical assistance and supervision during sleeping hours)
fha_claims.reasoning: Court applied the five-element FHA reasonable accommodation test and found plaintiff likely to succeed on the merits. The court determined the accommodation was necessary for equal opportunity to use and enjoy the dwelling, was reasonable because the aides must stay overnight to provide care and need sleep, and defendants had already acquiesced to the arrangement when plaintiff signed the lease in March 2022. The court rejected defendants' argument that HUD guidelines prohibited the accommodation, finding HUD guidelines are not mandatory and expressly allow reasonable accommodations in occupancy standards.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Rehabilitation Act, 29 U.S.C. § 794(a); Americans with Disabilities Act, 42 U.S.C. § 12132
fha_claims.reasoning: Court noted that standards under the ADA and Rehabilitation Act are similar to the FHA reasonable accommodation framework and applied the same analysis, finding plaintiff likely to succeed on the merits of her failure to accommodate claims under these statutes as well.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Reasonable accommodations to support disabled residents at the apartment complex, including safe and sanitary living conditions and accessible fire-evacuation routes for disabled residents
fha_claims.reasoning: This is a discovery dispute at the class-certification stage. The court did not reach the merits of the reasonable accommodation claim itself; rather, it ruled on what documents defendants must produce during discovery. The underlying FHA claims remain pending.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Title II claims; breach of duties imposed by common law and Kansas statutes regarding habitability and safe living conditions
fha_claims.reasoning: Non-FHA claims under the ADA and state law remain pending. The court's order addresses only discovery obligations and does not reach the merits of any substantive claim.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Safe and sanitary housing conditions; claims brought under Americans with Disabilities Act, Fair Housing Act, and Kansas common law and statutes for failure to maintain safe and sanitary conditions at apartment complex
fha_claims.reasoning: This opinion addresses a discovery dispute regarding attorney-client privilege and work-product protection for executed questionnaires. The court did not reach the merits of any FHA claim; the case involves habitability conditions and disability-related claims but the opinion concerns only privilege assertions in discovery, not substantive FHA liability.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Reasonable accommodation for elderly and disabled tenants regarding habitability conditions (bed-bug infestations, rodent bodies, flooding, leaking, mold)
fha_claims.reasoning: The court granted the motion to dismiss only Counts II (ADA) and VII (private nuisance). Count III, the FHA claim, was not addressed in the motion and survives the motion to dismiss, proceeding to the next stage.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: ADA Title II claim for failure to provide accessible accommodations in residential apartment complex
fha_claims.reasoning: The court held that the ADA does not apply to private residential apartment complexes, which are covered by the FHA instead. The plain language of the ADA regulates only 'public accommodations,' and residential apartments—even those catering to senior citizens—do not qualify as public accommodations under 42 U.S.C. § 12182.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Plaintiff alleges due process violation in eviction, equal protection violation, discrimination, invasion of privacy, defamation, and monopolization claims. Plaintiff also cites 42 U.S.C. § 3604 (FHA) but does not allege any disability or request any accommodation related to housing.
fha_claims.disposition: § 1915A(b) — frivolous and failure to state a claim
fha_claims.reasoning: The court conducted § 1915A screening and found the action legally frivolous because none of the defendants are state actors or acting under color of state law, which is a jurisdictional prerequisite for § 1983 liability. The court did not reach the merits of any claim, including the discrimination allegations, because the defendants are private parties and cannot be held liable under § 1983.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Removal of mold and cleaning of unit to accommodate rhinitis and breathing sensitivity
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to establish that rhinitis constituted a disability under the FHA, that Asset knew or should have known of any disability, that she requested an accommodation from Asset, or that Asset refused a reasonable accommodation. Asset hired a certified mold inspector who found no elevated mold levels, and Plaintiff never provided medical documentation to support her claims.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Professional mold remediation and cleaning of unit to accommodate rhinitis and breathing sensitivity
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to establish that her rhinitis constituted a disability, that Everest knew of any disability, or that Everest refused a reasonable accommodation. Everest cleaned Plaintiff's unit in response to her request and asked for medical documentation to verify the need for accommodation, which Plaintiff never provided. Plaintiff's subjective belief that professional cleaning was necessary was insufficient.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Remediation of excessive noise and transfer to a quiet apartment to accommodate PTSD and noise sensitivity
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to show that her requested accommodation was necessary, reasonable, or refused. Cardinal transferred Plaintiff to a ground-floor unit and emailed tenants about noise levels. Plaintiff could not identify the source of noise, referred to it as a 'ghost neighbor,' and provided no evidence of excessive noise. The accommodation is not 'indispensable' or 'essential' when Plaintiff continued to reside at the complex.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Alleged retaliation for seeking accommodation for rhinitis and mold sensitivity
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to establish protected activity (she did not request an accommodation from Asset) and failed to provide evidence of coercion, threats, intimidation, or interference. Asset was responsive to complaints and offered multiple options. Everest cleaned the unit and asked for medical documentation. No causal connection existed between any protected activity and adverse action.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Alleged retaliation for seeking accommodation for rhinitis and mold sensitivity
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to provide evidence of coercion, threats, intimidation, or interference by Everest. Her unsupported allegations that Everest insufficiently mitigated mold and her failure to provide medical documentation were insufficient to create a triable issue.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Alleged retaliation for seeking accommodation for PTSD and noise sensitivity, and for complaining about mold
fha_claims.reasoning: Although Cardinal's eviction could constitute interference, Plaintiff failed to establish a causal connection between her protected activity and the eviction. Cardinal transferred Plaintiff upon her first complaint and was responsive to other complaints. The eviction was for non-payment of rent, not retaliation for protected activity.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Alleged discrimination in unit assignment and treatment based on race and national origin
fha_claims.reasoning: Although Plaintiff is a member of a protected class (Black immigrant), she presented no evidence that Asset treated her differently because of her race or national origin. Her speculation that white tenants received nicer units based on peeking through a patio window and her belief-based allegations were insufficient to create a genuine issue of material fact.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Alleged discrimination and constructive eviction based on race and national origin
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff's allegation that Cardinal preferred white residents based on observation that 'so many tenants they have white race' was a statement of mere belief insufficient to create a genuine issue of material fact regarding intentional discrimination.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Intentional infliction of emotional distress, negligent infliction of emotional distress, failure to train/supervise/hire, and breach of implied warranty of habitability
fha_claims.reasoning: For IIED: Defendants' conduct was not extreme and outrageous; Asset and Everest were responsive to complaints. For NIED: Plaintiff presented no evidence of physical injury. For negligent hiring/training/supervision: Plaintiff failed to identify any employee who posed an undue risk of harm or any inadequate training. For breach of habitability: No evidence supported excessive mold or violation of housing laws; professional inspection found no elevated mold levels; Plaintiff continued to reside in units after alleged defects.

fha_claims.reasoning: The court granted class certification in part for issues 2-6 relating to defendants' standard of care and breach regarding bed bug infestations. The FHA claim survives as one of seven remaining claims after two claims were dismissed on motion. The opinion does not address the merits of the FHA claim itself, only whether class certification is appropriate for certain common issues.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: FHA violation claim (specific accommodation not identified in opinion); also includes implied warranty of habitability, breach of contract and statutory duty, failure to provide essential services, negligence, and Kansas Consumer Protection Act violation
fha_claims.reasoning: The opinion addresses only a motion for reconsideration of an evidentiary ruling at the class certification stage. The FHA claim and other claims remain pending; the court did not address the merits of any substantive claim in this opinion.

The complaint alleges bed bug infestations affecting elderly and disabled tenants.
fha_claims.reasoning: The court granted class certification in part for five of six proposed issues relating to defendants' standard of care and breach thereof regarding bed bug infestations. The FHA claim survives as one of seven remaining claims but has not been substantively analyzed on the merits; the opinion addresses only class certification procedural requirements under Rule 23.

source_file: 9710944_2023_HomeRoom, Inc. v. Shawnee, Kansas, City of_ksd

fha_claims.accommodation_description: 42 U.S.C. § 1983 substantive due process claim (right to intimate association and right to establish a home); Equal Protection claim under the Fourteenth Amendment; Kansas Zoning Enabling Act declaratory relief claim
fha_claims.reasoning: The court applied binding precedent from Village of Belle Terre v. Boraas, 416 U.S. 1 (1974), which established that municipalities may constitutionally limit the number of unrelated persons living together under rational basis scrutiny. The court found that plaintiffs' arguments elevate form over substance and that Belle Terre remains controlling authority. The state-law claim was dismissed for lack of supplemental jurisdiction after dismissal of all federal claims.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Providing correspondence to plaintiff in 18-point font and exempting plaintiff from online portal requirement for rent payment and maintenance requests; providing paper copy of annual lease
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff's claims regarding communications and rent payments were precluded under 42 U.S.C. § 3613(a)(2) because these requests were made in the prior administrative proceedings and formed the basis of the HUD complaint; plaintiff's only remedy is enforcement of the conciliation agreement, not a new FHA claim.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Repairs to unit including water damage, mold remediation, HVAC repair, plumbing repair, and other maintenance issues
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to allege that he requested an accommodation to an otherwise valid policy; rather, he merely complained about failure to perform routine maintenance repairs. The FHA requires a request for a change in policy or practice, not performance of landlord's basic maintenance obligations. Requests for repairs do not constitute reasonable accommodation claims under § 3604(f)(3)(B).

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Refusal to permit reasonable modifications to the unit
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to allege that he requested permission to make a reasonable modification at his own expense that defendants refused. The allegations focus on defendants' failure to perform maintenance, not on plaintiff's request for permission to modify the premises.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Misrepresentation that dwelling was not available for rental
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to allege that he was denied the opportunity to rent or negotiate rental of an apartment. Although AFI stated the lease would not be renewed, plaintiff continued to occupy the unit, was offered an alternative unit by OPG, and voluntarily vacated due to uninhabitable conditions—not because he was denied housing.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Retaliation for filing HUD complaint and exercising FHA rights, including failure to comply with conciliation agreement terms, failure to make repairs, and non-renewal of lease
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff sufficiently alleged a § 3617 retaliation claim by alleging: (1) disability and defendants' knowledge thereof; (2) protected activity (filing HUD complaint and entering conciliation agreement); (3) interference through violations of agreement terms, failure to make repairs, and lease non-renewal closely following protected conduct; and (4) discriminatory motive inferable from the pattern of conduct. The allegations are numerous, detailed, and not merely trivial disputes.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Rehabilitation Act discrimination and retaliation claims; Kansas Landlord Tenant Act claims; state law claims
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff's Rehabilitation Act claim failed because he alleged only conclusory facts that defendants received federal financial assistance without alleging any facts showing defendants received a subsidy from the federal government. Being a federal contractor is insufficient; the defendant must be a recipient of a subsidy. Property management compensation does not constitute federal financial assistance under the Rehabilitation Act.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Failure to provide reasonable accommodations related to pest control, habitability, and essential services for elderly and disabled tenants suffering from bed-bug infestations, mold, flooding, and other uninhabitable conditions
fha_claims.reasoning: The parties reached a settlement agreement resolving all FHA claims without judicial determination of merits. The settlement provides class members with monetary compensation of approximately $208.04 per month of residence and injunctive relief to remedy ongoing habitability issues at the property.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Implied warranty of habitability, breach of contract and statutory duty, failure to provide essential services, negligence, and Kansas Consumer Protection Act violations
fha_claims.reasoning: All non-FHA claims were resolved through the class settlement agreement without judicial determination of merits on the underlying legal theories.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Denial of opportunity to continue renting; alleged misrepresentation that unit was not available
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to allege that OPG and 37North had knowledge of his disability, and he was offered the opportunity to rent another unit but failed to attempt to rent it. The claim under § 3604(d) requires showing the housing opportunity remained available, which plaintiff did not establish.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Request for written confirmation of offer to transfer to another unit; requests for maintenance repairs characterized as accommodation requests
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to allege that OPG and 37North knew or reasonably should have known of his disability, and failed to allege that he requested an accommodation necessary to afford equal opportunity to use and enjoy the dwelling. Maintenance repair requests do not constitute reasonable accommodation requests under § 3604(f)(3)(B), which requires a change to an otherwise valid policy.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Alleged retaliation for complaints to HUD and local housing authority regarding maintenance issues
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff's protected activity (complaints to HUD and housing authority) occurred prior to OPG and 37North's ownership change, so he did not engage in protected activity regarding these defendants' actions. Additionally, plaintiff failed to allege that these defendants had knowledge of the protected activity.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Rehabilitation Act claim; Kansas Landlord Tenant Act claims for failure to maintain premises, unlawful entry, and retaliation
fha_claims.reasoning: Rehabilitation Act claim fails on same grounds as FHA claims (failure to allege knowledge of disability and failure to accommodate). Additionally, plaintiff failed to allege that OPG and 37North received federal financial assistance. KLTA claims fail because plaintiff failed to allege that 37North had knowledge of defects, OPG's request for vacation was reasonable given the state of disrepair, entries were made after plaintiff requested services, and retaliation claim lacks factual support.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Bivens claim for deliberate indifference to serious medical needs while incarcerated
fha_claims.disposition: Motion to Dismiss Denied Without Prejudice
fha_claims.reasoning: The court denied the defendant's motion to dismiss without prejudice after learning of the plaintiff's death. The case was not resolved on the merits but rather on the procedural issue of whether the plaintiff's mother would substitute as party pursuant to Rule 25 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: The court held that vacant land offered for sale for construction of residences qualifies as a 'dwelling' under 42 U.S.C. § 3604(b), and the plaintiffs' allegations that the city denied a zoning amendment to prevent development of affordable housing for Hispanics, Latinos, and other protected classes survived the motion to dismiss under the Iqbal/Twombly plausibility standard.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Takings Clause (Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments), conspiracy to commit unlawful taking
fha_claims.reasoning: The court dismissed the takings and conspiracy claims because the plaintiffs failed to allege pretext; condemnation of land for a public park is a universally recognized public use, and the plaintiffs did not allege that the city sought the property under mere pretext of public purpose to confer private benefit, as required under Kelo v. City of New London.

Ashcroft v. Iqbal, 556 U.S. 662 (2009)
Bell Atlantic Corp. v. Twombly, 550 U.S. 544 (2007)

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff's FHA disparate treatment claim based on gender and disabled status was time-barred under 42 U.S.C. § 3613(a)(1)(A), which requires civil action within 2 years of the discriminatory practice. The alleged discrimination occurred no later than July 24, 2020 (plaintiff's move-out date), but the complaint was not filed until August 11, 2022, exceeding the statute of limitations.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff's retaliation claim under 42 U.S.C. § 3617 against Detective Crump failed to plausibly allege discriminatory animus or disparate impact. The complaint contained only conclusory statements (e.g., alleged GPD policy of 'taking care of Georgetown's women,' alleged falsification of police report, alleged dropping of drug investigation) without supporting factual allegations sufficient to meet the Iqbal/Twombly plausibility standard.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Fraudulent misrepresentation, breach of contract, fraud by omission, breach of implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, tortious interference, statutory violations under U.S.C. Titles 24 and 42 (due process)
fha_claims.reasoning: All non-FHA claims failed under Rule 12(b)(6) for failure to state a plausible claim. Fraudulent misrepresentation claims lacked sufficient factual allegations of inducement; breach of contract claims failed because the lease imposed no obligation on Southern Oaks to enforce lease terms on plaintiff's behalf; fraud by omission failed because plaintiff did not plausibly allege the principal's identity was material to his decision to lease; breach of implied covenant failed because plaintiff admitted failing to complete recertification paperwork; tortious interference failed for the same reason; and statutory due process claims lacked legal basis and were merely regurgitations of statutory code.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: 42 U.S.C. § 1983 (deprivation of constitutional rights under color of law); 18 U.S.C. §§ 241, 242, 1621 (conspiracy, perjury, deprivation of rights); 42 U.S.C. § 3617 (cited but inapplicable)
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to plead sufficient factual allegations showing personal involvement of Defendants Bogan and Gregory in the alleged constitutional violation. The complaint contains only conclusory allegations and broad assertions unsupported by specific facts. Respondeat superior does not apply in § 1983 actions, and Plaintiff alleged no facts showing supervisory liability, authorization, approval, or acquiescence. Criminal statutes (18 U.S.C. §§ 241, 242, 1621) cannot be enforced by private citizens. Section 3617 (Fair Housing Act) has no applicability to the facts alleged.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Repair of broken apartment door that plaintiff alleged caused arm injury and mobility issues; plaintiff alleged he could not properly enter/exit apartment due to broken door requiring him to twist his arm
fha_claims.reasoning: Court allowed FHA reasonable accommodation claim to proceed against Chill, Hext, and Key Property Management without dismissing it; no substantive merits analysis was conducted at the screening stage.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court allowed FHA discrimination claim based on national origin and disability to proceed against Chill, Hext, and Key Property Management without substantive analysis at screening stage.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court allowed FHA retaliation claim under § 3617 to proceed against Chill, Hext, and Key Property Management; plaintiff alleged retaliation for filing HUD complaint and contacting Fair Housing Council.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: 42 U.S.C. § 1983 (due process/civil rights), Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (national origin discrimination), Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act (disability discrimination)
fha_claims.disposition: § 1983 claims dismissed under 28 U.S.C. § 1915(e)(2)(B); Title VI and § 504 claims survive
fha_claims.reasoning: § 1983 claims dismissed because defendants are private actors and § 1983 requires state action; Title VI and § 504 claims allowed to proceed against Chill, Hext, and Key Property Management as they do not require state action.

case_name: Ruth Castro Uribe v. Cynthia Ramser, et al.
key_cases_cited: Twombly, 550 U.S. 544
Kensu v. Corizon, Inc., 5 F.4th 646

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Plaintiff alleged housing rights violations, discrimination based on disability, race, ethnicity, age, and economic abuse; secondhand smoke exposure; requirement to provide twelve signed checks in advance; failure to maintain hot water; and alleged retaliation for notice to vacate. Claims were brought under Maine state law (22 M.R.S. § 3472) and Kentucky state law.
fha_claims.reasoning: Court dismissed for lack of subject matter jurisdiction because plaintiff failed to cite or allege any federal law or constitutional provision; complaint relied solely on Maine and Kentucky state law. To the extent plaintiff attempted to raise federal claims (including potential Fair Housing Act claims), they were dismissed without prejudice for failure to comply with Rule 8 because the complaint did not clearly identify any federal causes of action or develop factual allegations to support them.

case_name: Rodney L. Nance, Sr. v. Mayfield Plaza Apartments Management et al.
key_cases_cited: Ashcroft v. Iqbal
Bell Atl. Corp. v. Twombly
Lujan v. Defenders of Wildlife

fha_claims.accommodation_description: § 1983 Fourteenth Amendment due process claim; FHA claim based on alleged felon status discrimination
fha_claims.reasoning: Court dismissed § 1983 Fourteenth Amendment claim because defendants are private actors not acting under color of state law, and dismissed FHA claim because plaintiff is not a lessee, did not attempt to rent or buy an apartment, and felon status is not a protected class under the FHA. Court applied § 1915(e)(2)(B) screening standard and found claims frivolous or failing to state a claim.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Permission to keep emotional support animal (120-pound pit bull-Mastiff mix) off leash for training purposes during surgical recovery from knee surgery
fha_claims.disposition: Emergency Motion for Injunction Pending Appeal
fha_claims.reasoning: Court applied reasonableness balancing test and found the requested accommodation unreasonable because the dog had documented history of aggressive behavior toward residents, staff, and other animals, and allowing the dog off-leash would violate local ordinance and pose unacceptable risk of harm. The burden of the accommodation outweighed any benefits to plaintiff.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Transfer from current unit at 2903 Six Mile Lane to a single-family two-bedroom unit to accommodate emotional support animal safety during recovery from knee surgery
fha_claims.disposition: Emergency Motion for Injunction Pending Appeal
fha_claims.reasoning: Court found plaintiff failed to satisfy the necessity element because he did not provide required physician certification that the two-bedroom unit was medically necessary, despite LMHA's repeated requests and offer to arrange transfer if documentation was provided. Court also found no refusal element because LMHA conditioned the accommodation on reasonable verification, which plaintiff failed to obtain. LMHA offered alternative one-bedroom transfer which plaintiff rejected.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Plaintiff alleged retaliation for requesting reasonable accommodation, filing HUD complaint, and filing federal action
fha_claims.disposition: Emergency Motion for Injunction Pending Appeal
fha_claims.reasoning: Court found plaintiff could not establish causal connection between any protected activity and adverse action. Issues with unleashed dog and two-bedroom housing request predated HUD complaint and federal lawsuit. Eviction was based on failure to complete mandatory recertification (required of all tenants by lease and federal regulations) and alleged threats to LMHA employee, not protected activity.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Unlawful business practices under KRS § 367.110 and 42 U.S.C. § 3601; failure to engage in interactive process under ADA; disability discrimination under ADA, KCRA, and state law; unlawful business practices
fha_claims.disposition: Emergency Motion for Injunction Pending Appeal
fha_claims.reasoning: Court found unlawful business practices claim merely restated prior causes of action and failed for same reasons. Court rejected interactive process claim under ADA, noting FHA does not impose interactive process requirement and even if ADA requirement applied, LMHA engaged in good faith interactive process for over a year. Racial, gender, and age discrimination claims were waived as perfunctory allegations.

case_name: Watkins v. Commonwealth of Kentucky
key_cases_cited: Ashcroft v. Iqbal, 556 U.S. 662 (2009)
Bell Atl. Corp. v. Twombly, 550 U.S. 544 (2007)

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Plaintiff alleged violations of the Fourteenth Amendment, HUD regulations (42 CFR Title 42 Ch. 130 Sec. 231 and 212), and the Fair Housing Act in connection with eviction proceedings for non-payment of rent.
fha_claims.reasoning: The court dismissed under § 1915(e)(2)(B) as frivolous and for failure to state a claim. The FHA does not cover eviction for non-payment of rent, and plaintiff provided no factual allegations connecting her claims to any protected class or disability. The complaint was a legal conclusion unsupported by facts. Additionally, HUD regulations provide no private right of action, and § 1983 claims against the Commonwealth fail due to sovereign immunity and lack of personhood; claims against judges fail due to absolute judicial immunity; and claims against private parties fail because § 1983 requires state action.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Enforcement of HUD Smoke Free Rule against neighbor's smoking; secondhand smoke exposure
fha_claims.reasoning: The court determined that the Smoke Free Rule does not create a private cause of action for a neighboring tenant to sue based on a neighbor's smoking. The rule gives PHAs discretion to enforce but does not grant individual tenants a right to sue for violations. The FHA was invoked but the court found it inapplicable without substantive analysis of any FHA theory.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Denial of housing application based on pending drug-related criminal charges
fha_claims.disposition: Failure to state a claim under § 1915(e)(2)(B)
fha_claims.reasoning: The FHA does not prohibit discrimination based on criminal history. Plaintiff alleged denial based on pending drug-related criminal charges, which is not a protected class under 42 U.S.C. § 3604(a) (race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin). Additionally, 42 U.S.C. § 13661(c) explicitly permits public housing agencies to deny admission based on drug-related criminal activity.

case_name: Yusef Abdullah Bilal Ali v. Louisville Metro Housing Authority, et al.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Request to allow emotional support dog to be off-leash on LMHA property and common areas during recovery from knee surgery
fha_claims.reasoning: The court found that the plaintiff could not demonstrate the requested accommodation (off-leash dog) was reasonable given the dog's documented history of aggression toward residents, staff, and other animals. The defendant fairly determined the request was unreasonable under the balancing test.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Request to transfer to a single-family housing unit
fha_claims.reasoning: The court found that LMHA was amenable to the transfer and agreed to it subject to plaintiff providing physician certification that the transfer was medically necessary. Because plaintiff never provided the required documentation, he could not show the defendant refused the accommodation.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Failure to engage in interactive process regarding accommodation requests
fha_claims.reasoning: The court found that the FHA does not prohibit failure to engage in an interactive process. Even if analyzed under the ADA, the record demonstrated extensive interactive process engagement by defendants, including providing accommodation forms, offering transfers, explaining requirements, and continually offering assistance over more than a year.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Retaliation for requesting reasonable accommodation, failing to engage in interactive process, creating hostile living environment, filing HUD complaint, and filing this action
fha_claims.reasoning: The court found that plaintiff failed to point to any evidence demonstrating a causal connection between protected activity and adverse actions by defendants. Plaintiff provided no evidence that LMHA wrongly required recertification or improperly pursued eviction following threats against staff.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Unlawful business practices under KRS § 367.110 and 42 U.S.C. § 3601; disability discrimination under FHA, ADA, and KCRA; racial discrimination, gender discrimination, age discrimination under KCRA
fha_claims.reasoning: The unlawful business practices claim merely restated facts supporting other causes of action and failed for the same reasons. All non-FHA claims (KCRA discrimination claims, ADA claims, state law claims) were analyzed under the same substantive standards and failed on the merits.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: The court granted summary judgment on the § 3603(b)(2) 'Mrs. Murphy' exemption claim, finding that defendants do not qualify for the exemption because they do not own the building as a single individual or married couple; instead, each defendant owns only an individual unit with an undivided interest in common areas, which does not satisfy the ownership requirement of the exemption.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Discriminatory statement regarding familial status made in email by Haile after lease was signed
fha_claims.reasoning: The court granted summary judgment on the § 3604(c) claim because Haile's email statement about the Treeces' children was made after the lease was signed and did not concern the prospective sale or rental of an available dwelling; § 3604(c) applies only to discriminatory statements made during the rental process or in connection with prospective sales, not to statements made after housing has been occupied.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Imposition of daily fines, liens, attempted eviction, occupancy rule changes, lock changes on common storage shed, and installation of surveillance camera
fha_claims.reasoning: The court denied summary judgment on the § 3617 interference/coercion claim because material factual disputes exist regarding whether defendants interfered with plaintiffs' fair housing rights, including disputes over whether defendants imposed fines and liens to force eviction, changed occupancy rules, locked plaintiffs out of common areas, and installed surveillance cameras—all of which could constitute unlawful interference under § 3617.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Personal liability of individual defendants (Acuff, Jablonowski, Haile) for voting to authorize discriminatory actions and making discriminatory statements
fha_claims.reasoning: The court denied summary judgment on personal liability claims against individual defendants because material factual disputes exist regarding whether they personally participated in discriminatory acts through voting on discriminatory policies, making discriminatory statements to plaintiffs, and authorizing the association to take discriminatory actions such as imposing fines, pursuing eviction, and installing surveillance.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: The court found disputed material facts regarding whether defendant misrepresented the availability of her condominium unit to plaintiffs based on their familial status (family of six with three small children). The defendant's statement that the current tenant's lease extended through September 28 was contradicted by the tenant's testimony that he informed defendant of his August 23 move-out date twelve days before that statement. The court held that subtle discrimination questions are best resolved by a jury, and the timeline of events (accepting other applications five days after the misrepresentation) supported a reasonable inference of intentional discrimination based on familial status.

fha_claims.reasoning: The court denied defendants' motion for summary judgment on the disparate impact claim under § 3604(a), finding that plaintiffs established a prima facie disparate impact by showing that renter families with children are 30.5 to 104.7 times as likely to be affected by the occupancy limit as renter households without children, and that the comparison of rejection rates (rather than acceptance rates) is the proper methodology for analyzing disparate impact under the FHA.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Claim that defendants attempted to evict the Treeces based on familial status and attempted to force Harlan to evict the Treeces based on familial status
fha_claims.reasoning: The court granted defendants' motion for summary judgment on plaintiffs' § 3617 retaliation claim (referenced in the opinion as a separate motion), though the opinion does not provide detailed reasoning on this specific claim as it focuses primarily on the disparate impact analysis and the motion for reconsideration.

fha_claims.reasoning: Court found plaintiff failed to allege sufficient facts to state claims under ADA (no disability alleged, no public accommodation or public entity involvement), Title VI (no race, color, or national origin discrimination alleged), Title VII (no employment relationship or protected class discrimination alleged), or state law breach of contract (no contractual relationship pled). fha_claims.reasoning: The court dismissed claims against the Louisiana Department of Justice and Attorney General Jeff Landry under the Eleventh Amendment for lack of subject matter jurisdiction. The Fifth Circuit has held that Congress did not clearly intend to abrogate States' Eleventh Amendment sovereign immunity from suits under the Fair Housing Act, and Louisiana has not consented to suit in federal court.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Plaintiff cited FHA statutory provisions (42 U.S.C. §§ 3601, 3603, 3604) but alleged no facts supporting any FHA claim; no specific accommodation or discrimination theory articulated.
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff cited FHA provisions but failed to allege any facts demonstrating discrimination in rental or sale of a dwelling based on handicap, race, color, religion, sex, familial status, or national origin. The complaint contained only conclusory legal citations without factual support, failing to state a plausible claim under Iqbal/Twombly.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: ADA, Title VI, Title VII, and state law claims (rent overcharges, threats, unlawful acts)
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to allege adequate facts to support claims under the ADA, Title VI, Title VII, or state law. The amended complaint contained only incomprehensible assertions, unrelated documentation (cashier's checks, utility bills), and a request for a federal gun permit unrelated to the defendants or the housing dispute. The court found no factual allegations supporting any federal or state law cause of action.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiffs failed to establish the robust causation element required under ICP II and Lincoln Property. Although plaintiffs showed a substantial statistical disparity in the effect of the 250 and 400 square foot occupancy limits on families with children, they did not prove the occupancy limits caused families with children to be the dominant group affected by the policy; rather, families with children were a pre-existing condition of larger households, not created by the challenged policy.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Coercion, intimidation, and interference with exercise of FHA rights under § 3617 based on alleged violation of § 3604(a)
fha_claims.reasoning: Under Fifth Circuit precedent (Hood v. Pope and McZeal v. Ocwen Financial Corporation), a § 3617 retaliation claim requires an underlying violation of §§ 3603, 3604, 3605, or 3606. Because plaintiffs failed to establish a prima facie disparate impact claim under § 3604(a), their § 3617 claim based on that violation must also fail.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court applied Iqbal/Twombly plausibility standard and found that plaintiff's allegations of a single incident of unwanted touching of intimate body parts, even if isolated, is sufficient at the pleading stage to state a hostile housing environment claim under FHA § 3604(b), as the Fifth Circuit has held that deliberate and unwanted touching of intimate body parts can constitute severe sexual harassment, and plaintiff alleged the conduct interfered with her use and enjoyment of the property.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: State-law tort claims for sexual assault and battery; Louisiana Equal Housing Opportunity Act (LEHOA) claim
fha_claims.reasoning: Court denied motion to dismiss on supplemental jurisdiction grounds; state-law claims survive as supplemental to the federal FHA claim under 28 U.S.C. § 1367(a).

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court granted summary judgment on Dwayne and Phallon Treece's claim under § 3604(d) against Haile for representing that her unit was unavailable when it was actually available based on familial status. The claim was adjudicated on the merits.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court granted summary judgment on all plaintiffs' claim under § 3604(c) against all defendants for printing and publishing statements indicating occupancy limitations or discrimination based on familial status. The claim was adjudicated on the merits.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court granted summary judgment on all plaintiffs' disparate impact claim under § 3604(a) against all defendants for adopting occupancy limitations that have a disproportionate effect on families with children. The court found defendants entitled to summary judgment on this theory.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court modified its February 12, 2021 order to clarify that all plaintiffs' claims against all defendants for intentional disparate treatment discrimination under § 3604(a) in adopting occupancy limitations remain pending and were not addressed on the merits in the summary judgment order. These claims survive and are set for trial.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court clarified that Harlan's claims against all defendants under § 3604(a) for disparate treatment discrimination in refusing to allow him to sell his unit by discriminating against prospective buyers remain pending and were not addressed on the merits. These claims survive and are set for trial.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court clarified that Harlan's claims against all defendants under § 3604(b) for discrimination in the terms, conditions, or privileges of sale or rental based on familial status remain pending and were not addressed on the merits. These claims survive and are set for trial.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court modified its February 12, 2021 order to clarify that all plaintiffs' § 3617 claims for unlawfully coercing, intimidating, threatening, or interfering with plaintiffs in the exercise of their FHA rights remain pending because underlying violations of § 3604(a) and (b) are still pending. These claims survive and are set for trial.

fha_claims.reasoning: Court found that the complaint failed to allege sufficient facts to state a plausible claim against the individual defendants under the Fair Housing Act because it did not allege they acted outside the scope of their employment; under Meyer v. fha_claims.accommodation_description: Alleged retaliation for reporting JPHA to HUD; plaintiff claims she was terminated from FSSP program after threatening to report
fha_claims.reasoning: Court found that the complaint failed to allege sufficient facts to state a plausible claim against the individual defendants under the Fair Housing Act because it did not allege they acted outside the scope of their employment; under Meyer v. Holley, vicarious liability applies to the corporate employer, not individual employees acting within scope of employment.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Breach of contract claim for money owed under Jefferson Parish Family Self Sufficient Program (FSSP); § 1983 or state contract law
fha_claims.reasoning: Court found that the complaint failed to provide a short and plain statement of the claim and did not allege any facts regarding what actions the individual defendants took that would entitle plaintiff to relief; the complaint did not establish that the individual defendants were parties to the FSSP contract or what they specifically did to breach it.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Video remote interpreting (VRI) services and interpretive assistance for deaf residents; facility refused to provide or consider VRI despite receiving federal funds mandating non-discrimination and effective communication methods
fha_claims.reasoning: Court found that plaintiff's allegations of ownership, provision of residential care, employee refusal to accommodate deaf residents, and agency relationship were sufficient to survive motion to dismiss under Twombly plausibility standard; detailed factual allegations not required at pleading stage, only enough facts to raise reasonable expectation that discovery will reveal evidence of liability.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Americans with Disabilities Act Title III (42 U.S.C. § 12181 et seq.) - discrimination by owners/operators of places of public accommodation; Louisiana negligent hiring and supervision tort
fha_claims.reasoning: Court held that under ADA Title III, defendants who own or lease public accommodations may be held liable for discrimination, including vicarious liability for agents' actions; allegations that moving defendants own the facility (a place of public accommodation) and that employees refused interpretive services based on disability were sufficient to state a claim. Louisiana negligent hiring and supervision claim survived because plaintiff alleged ownership, agency relationship, and failure to provide reasonable accommodations.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: In-person or video remote interpreting (VRI)-assisted American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation for deaf residents
fha_claims.reasoning: The court found that plaintiff adequately alleged a claim under FHA § 3604(f)(3)(B) by alleging that movants, as owners/operators of a dwelling (nursing home), refused to make reasonable accommodations (ASL interpretation services) necessary to afford deaf prospective residents equal opportunity to enjoy the dwelling. The court did not apply the substantive reasonable accommodation balancing test, as the motion to dismiss was denied at the pleading stage.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Rehabilitation Act § 504 (denial of benefits in federally-funded program based on disability); Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act § 18116 (discrimination in health programs receiving federal financial assistance); Louisiana negligent supervision and training under La. C.C. art. 2315
fha_claims.reasoning: The court found that plaintiff adequately alleged claims under the Rehabilitation Act and ACA by alleging that movants denied benefits to otherwise-qualified deaf prospective residents based on disability at a federally-funded facility, and under Louisiana law by alleging movants owed a duty to provide equal opportunity and breached that duty by failing to provide interpretive services. The court applied the pleading standard (Iqbal/Twombly), not substantive merits analysis.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Americans with Disabilities Act Title III (denial of equal goods, services, facilities, privileges, advantages, accommodations, or other opportunities based on known disability of person with whom defendant has relationship or association)
fha_claims.reasoning: The court found that plaintiff adequately alleged an ADA Title II claim by alleging that movants own, operate, or manage a place of public accommodation (nursing home) and that employees engaged in discriminatory behavior by refusing to offer adequate interpretive services to prospective residents based on known disability. The court applied the pleading standard, not substantive merits analysis.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: The court applied the McDonnell Douglas burden-shifting framework and found that plaintiffs established a prima facie case of familial status discrimination under § 3604(a) by showing: (1) membership in protected familial class; (2) qualification to rent; (3) defendants made housing unavailable through threats/acts of eviction; and (4) housing remained available to similarly situated non-protected individuals. Material factual disputes exist regarding defendants' intent and whether their non-discriminatory reasons (infrastructure/quality of life concerns) were pretextual, precluding summary judgment.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Harlan failed to establish a prima facie case under §§ 3604(a) and (b) for discrimination against prospective buyers because he provided no evidence of any prospective buyer who was a member of the protected familial class. His deposition testimony only referenced prospective buyers refusing to purchase due to liens and litigation, not the occupancy limit, and was unsubstantiated speculation.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Under Hood v. Pope, § 3617 claims require an underlying violation of §§ 3603-3606. The court granted partial summary judgment on Harlan's § 3617 claims to the extent they were based on his failed §§ 3604(a) and (b) claims regarding prospective buyers. However, the court denied summary judgment on the remaining § 3617 claims based on the Treeces' underlying § 3604(a) claim, which survived summary judgment due to disputed material facts regarding intent and pretext.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: The time for dispositive motions on Claims 4 and 5 passed without defendants filing motions. These claims remain pending for trial, alleging that Haile refused to rent her unit to the Treeces based on familial status under § 3604(a).

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: The time for dispositive motions on Claims 4 and 5 passed without defendants filing motions. This claim remains pending for trial, alleging that Haile misrepresented the availability of her unit based on familial status under § 3604(d).

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: The court accepted as true that the criminal background screening policy disproportionately affects applicants based on race and that statistical data makes this plausible. Although the racial disparity is theoretical and speculative at the pleading stage, the court resolved ambiguity in the controlling law in plaintiff's favor regarding whether a disparate impact claim may be grounded on the 'predictably will cause' aspect of discriminatory effect under the 2013 HUD regulation. The motion to dismiss was denied as to the race disparate impact claim.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Reasonable accommodation for individuals recovering from drug addiction who are disabled under the FHA
fha_claims.reasoning: The disability claim failed to state a plausible claim because LaFHAC provided no statistical data suggesting that individuals with drug convictions are likely to be recovering from drug addiction that substantially limits major life activities, nor any data showing a causal link between the policy and disparate impact on disabled persons. The court found the claim lacked the 'robust' causal connection required by controlling law and dismissed for failure to state a claim.

source_file: 9721178_2022_Huber v. Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Florida, Inc._laed

fha_claims.accommodation_description: ADA wrongful termination claim based on disability (hemiplegic migraines); ADA failure to accommodate claim for use of CBD oil to manage migraines; ADA interference/coercion claim under 42 U.S.C. § 12203(b); LEDL wrongful termination and failure to accommodate claims
fha_claims.reasoning: Court found genuine disputes of material fact precluding summary judgment on all claims: (1) whether passing a drug test was an essential job function for plaintiff's position; (2) whether plaintiff was actually under the influence of illegal substances or whether the positive result was a false positive from legally prescribed CBD oil; (3) whether defendant's stated reason for termination was pretextual given the high healthcare costs of plaintiff's disability and her transition to a position not requiring drug testing; and (4) whether defendant provided good faith consideration of plaintiff's explanation for the positive drug test result as required for a reasonable accommodation. The court applied the McDonnell Douglas burden-shifting framework and found that plaintiff's prima facie case, combined with evidence of pretext and fact issues regarding the accommodation, survived summary judgment.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Provision of qualified American Sign Language (ASL) interpreters and/or Video Remote Interpreting (VRI) services for deaf residents
fha_claims.reasoning: The court found that plaintiff adequately alleged that movants own/operate the facility, that the facility is a dwelling under the FHA, that employees refused to make reasonable accommodations for prospective deaf residents, and that employees acted as movants' agents. These allegations sufficiently state a claim under 42 U.S.C. § 3604(f)(3)(B) and survive the motion to dismiss.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Rehabilitation Act § 504, ACA § 1557, ADA Title III, Louisiana negligent hiring and supervision
fha_claims.reasoning: The court found that plaintiff adequately alleged all elements required under the Rehabilitation Act (qualifying disability, otherwise qualified, denial of benefits solely by reason of disability, federal financial assistance), ACA (same framework as Rehabilitation Act), ADA (movants own/operate public accommodation, employees discriminated based on known disability, employees acted as agents), and Louisiana negligent supervision (duty, breach, causation, legal cause). All non-FHA claims survive the motion to dismiss.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Plaintiff alleged discrimination based on disability and familial status in connection with termination from Housing Choice Voucher Program and forfeiture of Family Self-Sufficiency Program escrow funds.
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to file opposition to summary judgment motion and presented no evidence of discriminatory intent or effect. Court found JPHA entitled to judgment as a matter of law because plaintiff could not establish prima facie case of discrimination under FHA.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Plaintiff alleged retaliation for exercising FHA rights and contacting parties about discrimination and privacy violations.
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to file opposition and presented no evidence that JPHA's termination decision was causally linked to protected activity or motivated by retaliation. Court applied three-element retaliation test and found plaintiff could not satisfy burden.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Breach of contract/unjust enrichment claim for funds allegedly owed under Jefferson Parish Family Self-Sufficiency Program escrow account.
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to dispute that she was properly terminated from HCVP for failing to timely report income and failing to disclose marriage. Under program regulations, escrow funds revert to housing authority upon participant termination, and JPHA presented undisputed evidence of proper termination.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court denied summary judgment without prejudice under Rule 56(d) because plaintiff could not adequately oppose the motion without completing discovery regarding Mai's involvement in management and the discriminatory policy. Evidence showed Mai was authorized to enter lease agreements and fired Sponberg, creating material disputes of fact requiring further discovery.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Louisiana Equal Housing Opportunity Act claims (three counts)
fha_claims.reasoning: Court denied summary judgment without prejudice on state law claims under the same Rule 56(d) analysis, finding material disputes of fact regarding Mai's involvement in management and the discriminatory policy that require further discovery before summary judgment can be properly decided.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: No FHA claims alleged. Plaintiff brought claims under La. Rev. Stat. § 51:2247 (Louisiana Human Rights Act), La. Rev. Stat. § 49:146 (Louisiana public accommodations statute), and Title II of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 for alleged discrimination based on race and sex in denial of entry to casino.
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to plausibly allege discrimination under Iqbal/Twombly standard. Allegations that defendant's refusal to accept military ID was based on race or gender were conclusory and speculative, with no non-conclusory facts connecting defendant's statements about the ID being 'fake' to plaintiff's race or gender. Pattern-or-practice allegations based on two isolated incidents were insufficient to establish a pattern or practice of discrimination.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Housing segregation and isolation of Filipino workers in bunkhouse and COVID-19 quarantine accommodations based on national origin, while non-Filipino workers were not subjected to the same restrictions.
fha_claims.disposition: Motion to Compel Arbitration — Denied as to FHA claim
fha_claims.reasoning: The court determined that plaintiffs' FHA disparate treatment claims based on national origin discrimination in housing assignments do not fall within the scope of the narrow arbitration clause (which covers only disputes 'arising from' employment) because the claims could be maintained independently of the employment contract and are not a foreseeable result of the parties' contractual duties. The court declined to compel arbitration, allowing the FHA claim to proceed in federal court.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: TVPA forced labor claims; § 1983 due process claims (if any); state tort claims related to confinement, threats of deportation, and unsafe housing conditions
fha_claims.disposition: Motion to Compel Arbitration — Denied as to TVPA and other non-FHA claims
fha_claims.reasoning: The court held that plaintiffs' TVPA forced labor claims do not arise from employment under the narrow arbitration clause because the alleged violations (confinement in bunkhouse after employment contract ended, threats of deportation, unsafe conditions) are independent of the employment relationship and not a foreseeable result of contractual duties. The claims could be maintained independently of the employment contract and thus fall outside the scope of arbitration.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Waiver of apartment animal fee and weight restriction to allow plaintiff's 35-pound emotional support dog to live in the apartment
fha_claims.disposition: Rule 41(b) Motion to Dismiss for Failure to Prosecute
fha_claims.reasoning: The court denied defendant's motion to dismiss for failure to prosecute under Rule 41(b), finding no clear record of contumacious conduct and noting that the prior arbitration order lacked a specific deadline. The underlying FHA reasonable accommodation claim survives and remains pending, subject to plaintiff's obligation to initiate arbitration within 30 days or face dismissal with prejudice.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Fair Housing Act claim mentioned in amended reconventional demand but not substantively addressed by the court
fha_claims.reasoning: The court lacked subject matter jurisdiction over the action. Bacot's federal counterclaims, including the Fair Housing Act claim, cannot serve as the basis for federal question jurisdiction under the well-pleaded complaint rule. The original complaint raised no federal questions, and Bacot as a forum defendant could not invoke diversity jurisdiction. The court therefore did not reach the merits of any federal claims.

fha_claims.reasoning: The court did not reach the merits of the reasonable accommodation claim because it found the Anti-Injunction Act barred injunctive relief based on the FHA claim. The claim survives the procedural challenge to the preliminary injunction motion but has not been substantively decided on the merits.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Parish ordinance restricting number of unrelated individuals in single-family homes and requiring permits for addictive disorder treatment facilities
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiffs alleged the Parish's ordinances had a discriminatory impact on group homes for disabled individuals, but the court did not reach the merits because the Anti-Injunction Act barred injunctive relief based on the FHA claim.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Parish's filing of state court injunction action after Plaintiffs requested reasonable accommodation
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiffs alleged retaliation under the FHA for requesting accommodation, but the court did not reach the merits because the Anti-Injunction Act barred injunctive relief based on the FHA claim.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: ADA Title II claim for discrimination based on disability; Rehabilitation Act § 504 claim for discrimination based on handicap; 42 U.S.C. § 1983 claim for retaliation against First Amendment right to petition government
fha_claims.reasoning: The court found the Anti-Injunction Act barred injunctive relief based on the ADA and RA claims. For the § 1983 retaliation claim, the court found Plaintiffs failed to establish a likelihood of success on the merits because the Parish's enforcement action predated any indication that Plaintiffs would request accommodation, breaking the causal chain required for retaliation.

fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to allege facts supporting elements two through four of the prima facie disparate treatment test (that she applied and was qualified, was rejected, and housing remained open to similarly situated applicants). The complaint contained only conclusory allegations and was devoid of factual support for a § 3604 claim.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: State law claims arising from the same transaction (unsafe structures enforcement action in state court)
fha_claims.reasoning: The action is barred by the doctrine of res judicata because all elements are satisfied: valid final judgment from state court, same parties (reversed roles), and the FHA claims arose out of the same transaction and should have been asserted as a compulsory reconventional demand in the state court proceeding. Additionally, the Rooker-Feldman doctrine precludes federal court review of state court judgments.

fha_claims.disposition: Not directly addressed; case involves arbitration motion and defamation counterclaim dismissal
fha_claims.reasoning: The FHA claim survived the motion to compel arbitration (court denied arbitration as to FHA claims), but this opinion addresses only the defamation counterclaim and does not reach the merits of the underlying FHA discrimination claim regarding segregated housing assignments.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: FLSA minimum wage and overtime violations; TVPA forced labor and trafficking claims; refusal to allow evacuation during Hurricane Ida
fha_claims.disposition: Motion to compel arbitration granted as to FLSA; denied as to TVPA and FHA
fha_claims.reasoning: FLSA claims were stayed pending arbitration; TVPA and FHA claims survived the arbitration motion and remain pending in federal court. This opinion does not address the merits of any non-FHA claims, only the procedural arbitration ruling and the defamation counterclaim.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Reasonable accommodation for emotional support animals
fha_claims.reasoning: The court granted defendants' motion to strike plaintiff's jury demand based on a valid jury waiver clause in the lease agreement. The underlying FHA reasonable accommodation claim for emotional support animals remains pending; this order addresses only the procedural issue of jury trial waiver and does not reach the merits of the FHA claim.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Waiver of no-pet policy to allow plaintiff to keep two pit bulls as emotional support animals for anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress disorder, chemical seizures, and agoraphobia
fha_claims.reasoning: Court found genuine issues of material fact precluding summary judgment on whether defendants knew or should have known of plaintiff's disability (second element satisfied by plain language of accommodation request letter) and whether defendants refused the accommodation (April 5 letter constituted refusal despite 'at this time' language, and notice to vacate with eviction proceedings constituted punishment for animals' presence).

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court found genuine issue of material fact on causal connection element: plaintiff engaged in protected activity (request for reasonable accommodation), suffered adverse action (eviction filing), and notice to vacate cited both non-payment of rent and 'unauthorized animals' as lease violations, creating factual dispute over whether retaliation was the motivating factor.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Louisiana Equal Housing Opportunity Act (LEHOA) violation, negligent hiring, training, and supervision under Louisiana law
fha_claims.reasoning: Court explicitly stated that defendants' motion for summary judgment addressed only FHA claims and did not address plaintiff's LEHOA or negligent training claims; court made no findings as to non-FHA claims.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court found Hughes plausibly alleged racial discrimination under § 3604(a) by alleging Bouchon made racial remarks, sent derogatory messages, and evicted him based on race rather than unpaid rent. All four elements of disparate treatment (protected class membership, qualification to rent, rejection, unit available to others) were sufficiently pleaded to survive 12(b)(6).

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Court dismissed § 3604(c) discriminatory advertising claim because the complaint alleged no facts showing Bouchon made, printed, or published any notice or advertisement indicating preference or discrimination. All allegations centered on eviction and refusal to rent, which fall outside § 3604(c)'s scope.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Reasonable modifications or accommodations related to disability; specific nature of accommodation not alleged
fha_claims.reasoning: Court dismissed § 3604(f)(3)(B) reasonable accommodation claim because Hughes failed to allege sufficient nexus between his disability and the eviction, did not allege a specific accommodation was requested, did not allege he funded or offered to fund modifications, and did not allege any accommodation was necessary or reasonable. Conclusory allegations of refusal to accommodate were insufficient under Iqbal/Twombly.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: 42 U.S.C. § 1982 racial discrimination claim; state law claims (eviction, breach of contract, harassment, tortious interference, etc.)
fha_claims.reasoning: Court denied motion to dismiss § 1982 claim, finding Hughes plausibly alleged Bouchon's racial animus (racial remarks, derogatory text), intentional discrimination, and that eviction was motivated by race. Court retained supplemental jurisdiction over state law claims.

fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff failed to adequately plead the fourth element of reverse redlining (that defendant intentionally targeted him for unfair loans or makes loans on more favorable terms to others). Plaintiff's allegations demonstrate he sought out the loan and defendant did not actively induce him, failing to plead the required elements for reverse redlining.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: Fraud, unjust enrichment, Title VII employment discrimination, UDAP, CSA, UTPCPL, § 1983
fha_claims.reasoning: Fraud claim dismissed without prejudice for failure to satisfy Rule 9(b) particularity requirement but granted leave to amend. Unjust enrichment claim dismissed with prejudice because Louisiana law precludes unjust enrichment when another remedy is available. Miscellaneous claims (Title VII, UDAP, CSA, UTPCPL) not properly pled with factual support or viable legal foundation.

fha_claims.accommodation_description: N/A
fha_claims.reasoning: Plaintiff's original FHA claims alleging racial discrimination in making available residential real estate transactions and in terms/conditions of such transactions were dismissed with prejudice in the first motion to dismiss for failure to state a plausible claim under Iqbal/Twombly.
